q: 1. Who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 2026?
explain: Navanethem 'Navi' Pillay was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her contribution to bringing those involved in war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide within the scope of the law, and to strengthening international law.

q: 2. Which is the first country with whom Nepal has established formal diplomatic relation?
explain: Nepal established its first formal diplomatic relations with the United Kingdom on May 17, 1816, following the Treaty of Sugauli.

q: 3. Which is the latest country with whom Nepal has established formal diplomatic relation?
explain: As per the current records in the provided material, Kiribati is the most recent addition to the list of countries maintaining diplomatic ties with Nepal.

q: 4. Which is the First SAARC country with whom Nepal has established formal diplomatic relation?
explain: Nepal and India established formal diplomatic relations on June 13, 1947.

q: 5. Who was the prime minister of Nepal at the time of diplomacy with Pakistan?
explain: Diplomatic relations with Pakistan were established in 1960, during the premiership of B.P. Koirala.

q: 6. Which one of the following is not constructed with the aid of Japan?
explain: Udaypur Cement Industries Limited was established with the assistance of the Government of Japan, however, in the context of this specific exam key, it is listed as the outlier.

q: 7. Which of the following was not constructed by the Russian government's assistance?
options: Pathalaiya - Dhalkebar Segment of Mahendra Highway

q: 8. Which of the following was not constructed by the Chinese government's assistance?

q: 9. When did UNO came into existence?
explain: The UN officially came into existence on October 24, 1945, after the Charter was ratified by the five permanent members of the Security Council and a majority of other signatories.

With Iraq not yet fully ready to take over security, it is noted that the US withdrawal creates a vacuum and carries the risk of reviving extremist groups such as the Islamic State.

q: 11. Branches of which tree appear on the UN flag?
explain: The UN flag contains olive branches, which symbolize peace.

q: 12. Who coined the name of "United Nations"?
explain: The name 'United Nations' was coined by U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt in the Declaration by United Nations of January 1, 1942.

q: 13. The last country to sign the Charter of UNO was --------
explain: Poland was not at the San Francisco conference but left a space to sign as the 51st original member later.

q: 14. The UN Charter is concerned with ---------
explain: The UN Charter is the binding constitutional document for all bodies and member states of the UN.

q: 15. Currently, How many countries have signed the CITES treaty?
explain: As of recent counts reflected in the textbook, 184 parties (including the EU) have joined the CITES treaty.

q: 16. Which one of the following is/are a function(s) of the UN General Assembly?
options: Any matter affecting International peace & Security
It passes UN budget of the UN.
It elects the Non- permanent members of the Security Council
explain: The General Assembly has the authority to discuss security, approve budgets, and elect non-permanent members of the Security Council.

q: 17. Who is the person to deliver the longest speech in the General Assembly?
explain: Fidel Castro holds the record for the longest speech at the UN General Assembly, lasting 4 hours and 29 minutes in 1960.

q: 18. Which of the following organs of the United Nations Organization elects judges of the International court of Justice?
options: The Security Council and the General Assembly
The trusteeship council and the economic and social council
explain: Judges of the ICJ are elected simultaneously by the General Assembly and the Security Council.

q: 19. In which year was Nepal first elected on a Non-Permanent member of the united Nation Security Council?
explain: Nepal served its first term as a non-permanent member of the Security Council during the 1969-1970 term.

q: 20. How many members are there in the International Court of Justice and what is their tenure?
explain: The Court is composed of 15 judges elected for nine-year terms by the UN General Assembly and the Security Council.

q: 21. Which One of the following is the main objective of Vienna Convention and its Montreal protocol?
explain: The Vienna Convention and the Montreal Protocol are international agreements specifically designed to phase out substances that deplete the ozone layer.

q: 22. Why did the Trusteeship Council suspend its operation?
options: Due to the used of USA veto
due to completion of its mandate
due to disputes between Member States
explain: The Council's mission was to oversee the transition of trust territories to self-government or independence; it suspended operations because its mandate was fulfilled.

q: 23. Which Secretary General of UN presented The Quiet Revolution Concept Paper?
explain: Kofi Annan presented 'The Quiet Revolution' as a series of reforms to renew the United Nations in 1997.

q: 24. Which organ of the United Nations cannot be attended by the Secretary General of the United Nations?
explain: While the SG serves as the chief administrative officer of most organs, the ICJ is an independent judicial body.

q: 25. For how many years is the Secretary General's working period at a time?
explain: The Secretary-General is appointed for a five-year term, which is renewable.

q: 26. At which article of United Nations Charter, establishment of specialized agencies are mentioned?
explain: Article 57 of the UN Charter provides for the establishment of specialized agencies through intergovernmental agreements.

q: 27. Which UN Organization became the first to accept a donation in crypto currency?
explain: UNICEF launched its CryptoFund in 2019, becoming the first UN organization to hold and make transactions in cryptocurrency.

q: 28. On which date did the SAPTA Agreement officially enter into force?
explain: SAPTA officially entered into force on December 7, 1995. September 28, 1993 is Nepal's ratification date; November 5, 1995 is Bangladesh's ratification date; January 1, 2006 is SAFTA's active date.

q: 29. Which of the following is not organ of United Nations?
explain: The IMF is a specialized agency, not one of the six principal organs of the United Nations.

q: 30. Which of the following is a World Bank group of five institutions?
explain: The International Development Association (IDA) is one of the five institutions that make up the World Bank Group.

q: 31. How many specific goods are scheduled under the SAPTA trade agreement?
explain: SAPTA contains 14 specific categories of goods subject to preferential trade. The other options are other numbers.

q: 32. Who signed the SAFTA agreement on behalf of the Government of Nepal?
explain: Dr. Bhesh Bahadur Thapa signed SAFTA on behalf of Nepal. Mahesh Acharya signed SAPTA; the others are Secretaries-General.

q: 33. Which of the following is not function of United Nations Development Program (UNDP)?
explain: The protection of refugees is the specific mandate of UNHCR, not UNDP.

q: 34. From which institution the concept of good governance has developed?
explain: The World Bank is credited with popularizing the concept of 'good governance' in the late 1980s as a condition for economic development.

q: 35. Where is United Nations University located?
explain: The United Nations University (UNU) is headquartered in Shibuya, Tokyo, Japan.

q: 36. Which of the following UN agencies has its headquarters at Paris -----------
explain: The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) is based in Paris, France.

q: 37. Which of the following is not an agency of UNO?
options: International Committee of the Red Cross
explain: The ICRC is an independent humanitarian institution and is not part of the UN system.

q: 38. The headquarters of World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) is located in -----------
explain: WIPO is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

q: 39. When ILO became a specialized agency of UN?
explain: While founded in 1919, the ILO became the first specialized agency of the UN in 1946.

q: 40. In which Country, UNO has spent highest quantity of Budget?
explain: Historically, in the context of these specific records, Haiti has seen significant UN spending due to humanitarian and peacekeeping efforts.

q: 41. In which year, UN celebrated international peace on?
explain: The UN observed 1986 as the International Year of Peace, aimed at strengthening peace-related efforts worldwide.

q: 42. When was Nepal elected to the UN Security Council as a non-permanent membership for the first time?
explain: Nepal first served as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council during 1969-1970.

q: 43. When did Nepal participate in United Nations peace-keeping force as an observer for the first time?
explain: Nepal first participated as an observer in a UN peacekeeping mission in 1958.

q: 44. Of which organization among the following has Nepal become the member at first?
explain: Nepal's earliest membership among these bodies was with the Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), joined shortly after independence-era engagement with the UN system.

q: 45. From which country, the concept of the rural Development bank was emerged?
explain: The rural development bank concept, notably the microfinance-based Grameen Bank model, originated in Bangladesh.

q: 46. Who is Current 4th Secretary General of BIMSTEC?
explain: As per this reference material, Indra Mani Pandey is listed as the 4th Secretary-General of BIMSTEC.
